name: Rudnick & Gao (2003), Treatise on Geochemistry 3, 1-64 -- bulk continental crust composition

source.located: Rudnick, R.L., Gao, S. (2003) 'Composition of the Continental Crust', Treatise on Geochemistry vol. 3, pp. 1-64, DOI 10.1016/B0-08-043751-6/03016-4. Not on arXiv. The chapter itself was NOT reached: alphaXiv returned 'assistant quota exceeded' on answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers; academia.edu, researchgate, ADS, semanticscholar, arxiv.org, uvic dspace and springeropen were all refused by the egress proxy (403, organization policy -- not retried or routed around).
source.via: pyrolite 0.3.7 (pip download from pypi, the allowlisted host) ships machine-readable transcriptions of R&G's tables: pyrolite/data/geochem/refcomp/BCC_RudnickGao2003.csv (md5 e01631fe8a352f899c5661afc797a7ce), UCC_RudnickGao2003.csv (545acc8ddbee2bba4829882bb996c23f), LCC_RudnickGao2003.csv, plus the 2014 second-edition files; extracted to d67/src/pyrolite_refcomp/. This is a third-party restatement, not an arXiv paper, and it carries one visible transcription fault: the BCC file's N row is empty and a row labelled 'Na, 56, ppm' sits among the traces although Na is a major (Na2O 3.1 %) -- read here as N = 56 ppm (the UCC file carries N 83 ppm in its N row). Major oxides in the restatement are given to 1 decimal (bulk SiO2 60.6, Al2O3 15.9, FeO 6.7, MgO 4.7, CaO 6.4, Na2O 3.1, K2O 1.8, TiO2 0.7, P2O5 0.1, MnO 0.1 wt%); whether the chapter prints more digits could not be READ. Later literature (Johnson & Goldblatt 2015, arXiv:1505.03813) is NAMED-NOT-READ.

published_statement: As restated (pyrolite BCC_RG2003, 'ModelType Calculation', 'Reservoir BulkContinentalCrust'): a recommended composition of the present-day bulk continental crust -- ten major oxides in wt% and ~70 trace elements in ppm/ppb, among them N 56 ppm (row mislabelled 'Na' in the restatement), S 404, Cl 244, F 553, Li 16, Zn 72, Cu 27, Cr 135, Ni 59, Co 26.6, Ba 456, Sr 320, Zr 132, V 138, Ta 0.7 ppm, Au 1.3 ppb, Ag 56 ppb; and a separate upper-crust (UCC) column with N 83 ppm, P2O5 0.15 %, TiO2 0.64 %, Zn 67, Cr 92, Ni 47, Co 17.3, As 4.8, Br 1.6, Y 21 ppm, Ag 53 ppb, Au 1.5 ppb. The restated table carries NO values for O, H, C (the O, H, C and N element rows are empty; H2O/CO2 are not among the oxides). The chapter's own wording and stated uncertainties were not READ.
published_hypotheses: Scope: the CONTINENTAL crust of the present-day EARTH only -- not oceanic crust, not the atmosphere/hydrosphere/biosphere, not any other body (reservoir label 'BulkContinentalCrust', title of the chapter).

The bulk value is a CALCULATION (restatement 'ModelType Calculation') combining separate upper, middle and lower crust estimates; the mixing proportions and the seismological model behind them were not READ here.
Volatiles: no H, C or O values are given; H2O and CO2 are not among the tabulated oxides (restatement). N, S, Cl, F are tabulated as traces.
Upper-crust and bulk-crust values are different quantities (e.g. N 83 vs 56 ppm; P2O5 0.15 vs 0.1 %; Zn 67 vs 72 ppm).
Uncertainties per element: NOT READ (the restatement's unc_2sigma column is empty for every row).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED -- scope extended from Earth's continental crust to 'a planet' / 'a rocky crust' destination: stock.py:4 ('a carbonaceous chondrite beats a planet'), stock.py:103-104 ('a planet differentiates'), stock.py:112 ('THE OPTIMAL ARRIVAL NODE IS AN ASTEROID, NOT A PLANET'), stockgate.py:26 ('An asteroid beats a planet. All of that stands'). R&G's quantity is one reservoir of one planet; it excludes the atmosphere, which holds most of Earth's surface-accessible nitrogen (78 % N2 by volume -- common knowledge, not READ here in a paper). The crust datum supports 'Earth's continental crust is a poor N stock'; it does not by itself support 'a planet is a poor destination'.

ADDED -- interpretive hypothesis that the crust's N scarcity is caused by differentiation/outgassing ('a silicate residue that outgassed its volatiles', stock.py:103-104; test label stock.py:499-500; 'Earth's crust outgassed', stockgate.py:177; the D25 conjunct 'primitive rather than devolatilised', stockgate.py:233, :802). R&G tabulate a concentration; the causal reading is the tree's and is not in the restated table. The CHECK at stock.py:499 only tests CRUST['N'] < CRUST['P'].

DRIFT IN THE NUMBERS ATTRIBUTED TO R&G, stock.py CRUST (stock.py:193-194 cites R&G, table at :211-214): of 16 entries only 5 (Si, Al, Na via oxide stoichiometry; Zn, Li as traces; each within 3 %) match R&G bulk; 8 match neither the bulk nor the upper-crust column (Fe 0.0563 vs 0.0521; Ca 0.0415 vs 0.0457; Mg 0.0233 vs 0.0283; K 0.0209 vs 0.0149; P 0.00105 vs 0.000436 bulk / 0.000655 upper; S 0.00035 vs 0.000404; Cl 0.00017 vs 0.000244; N 0.00006 vs 0.000056); 3 (O 0.461, C 0.002, H 0.0014) are values R&G do not tabulate at all. rederivation.outcome: (1) The owners' own numbers reproduce exactly from their own tables: stock.py crust binds N at 4.2805e2, N/P factor ratio 40.386, crust/chondrite 40.001; stockgate crust binds N at 4.5862e2; craft at crust binds Au at 2.6948e5. (2) Provenance against the restated R&G tables: stock.py CRUST 5 = R&G bulk, 8 match neither bulk nor upper, 3 not R&G quantities; stockgate CRUST 41 = bulk, 10 = upper, 5 neither, 4 not R&G quantities; R&G oxide stoichiometry gives O = 0.4641 vs tree 0.461. (3) Substituting R&G values: binding element stays N in both owners (bulk: 458.6, 32.10 t per 70 kg; upper: 309.4); chondrite still beats crust (42.86x bulk, 28.92x upper); craft still binds Au (2.695e5 / 2.335e5); stock.py's '40.4x N over P' becomes 17.98 (DISCREPANCY). (4) Thresholds: N stops binding above 225 ppm (C-limit) / 360 ppm (H-limit) at the tree's C, H; with N = 56 ppm, C would take over below 498 ppm crust C. (5) At the later upper-crust N of 150 ppm (NAMED-NOT-READ) N still binds at 171.2, crust/chondrite 16.0.

An independent compilation differing from R&G by factors up to ~2 in traces (e.g. Ba 250 vs 456, Cr 185 vs 135, Ni 128 vs 59 ppm) and carrying no N: crust compositions are compilation-dependent at the tens-of-percent level. None of these elements binds the human payload.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What R&G had in 2003: crustal N rests on sparse data (the chapter's own N discussion could not be READ here); what came later: R&G's own 2014 revision left N at 56/83 ppm, and Johnson & Goldblatt (2015; NAMED-NOT-READ) reportedly put upper-crust N at ~150 ppm, ~1.8x R&G's upper value. Does having that datum change the conclusion? COMPUTED here: it changes the magnitude (crust N factor 458.6 -> 171.2; crust/chondrite 42.9 -> 16.0) and not the binding element or the destination ranking -- N keeps binding until crust N exceeds 225 ppm. So on this result M's hypothesis is supported only in the weak sense that a datum moved; the tree's qualitative conclusion does not rest on the missing data. Evidence the other way: the larger inaccuracies found are not in R&G at all but in the tree's USE of it -- values labelled R&G that R&G do not print (stock.py P, C, H, O and four majors; stockgate's bulk/upper mixture), and the extension of a crust datum to 'a planet'. Those are drift, not a lack of data by the 2003 authors.
grade_evidence: Evidence FOR: from the restated R&G tables the tree's qualitative claims reproduce -- the continental crust binds a human payload on N (bulk 458.6, upper 309.4), a CI chondrite beats it (42.9x bulk, 28.9x upper), a craft payload binds on Au there (2.695e5) -- and they survive the one later datum found (N 150 ppm: still N, 16.0x). Evidence AGAINST 'STANDS': (a) the tree uses the result on a wider class than the source covers -- 'a planet' (stock.py:4, :103-104, :112; stockgate.py:26) where R&G describe Earth's continental crust only, excluding the atmosphere; (b) the N-binding claim carries an unstated hypothesis on crust C > 8.889 x crust N (> 498 ppm), and C is not an R&G quantity; (c) stock.py's '40.4x N over P' (stock.py:105-107, :506-508) does not reproduce from R&G's P (17.98) -- a discrepancy in the value attributed to R&G, recorded, not a refutation; (d) 8 of stock.py's 16 and 5 of stockgate's 60 crust values match neither R&G column, and stockgate mixes 10 upper-crust values into a table labelled 'bulk'. The source itself was READ only through a third-party machine transcription with one mislabelled row (N as 'Na'); no claim here says R&G are wrong. Not WRONG (nothing refuted), not OPEN (the table was readable by restatement and the arithmetic is checkable), and the magnitude is DATA-DEPENDENT on crustal N (contested 56/83/150 ppm) -- NARROWED is chosen because the binding consequences hold only under a hypothesis (crust-only destination, crust C above threshold) the tree does not state.
what_would_change_the_grade: Toward STANDS: the tree restricting the claim to 'Earth's continental crust' (not 'a planet'), stating the crust-C hypothesis with a READ crustal C value above 498 ppm, and re-citing or replacing the non-R&G values. Toward DATA-DEPENDENT: a READ crustal N above 225 ppm (C-limit at the tree's C) or a READ crustal C below 498 ppm would flip the binding element. Toward OPEN: if the chapter, READ at source, prints values differing from the pyrolite transcription beyond rounding. Reading the chapter (Table of recommended compositions) and Johnson & Goldblatt 2015 at source are the two outstanding reads.
